From: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@auroraveil.com>

Subject: Urgent — KV-cache starvation on our on-prem cluster (p99 spikes / 502s)

Marissa,

We're seeing a sustained degradation across our private on-prem cluster starting ~08:45 PST. Symptoms: p99 generation latency spiking to 4-8s (baseline ~200ms), ~15% 502s on model endpoints, and overall throughput collapsed to ~40% of normal. This started right after we pushed a moderate traffic increase for a marketing push.

We run the Redwood Private build you shipped last quarter (version 1.9.2) in our VPC with 3 replicas. Attached are a 10MB sample of KV/serve logs and a short CPU profile. Our CTO (Matthew) and Board have asked for an executive-level update by EOD PST — they are concerned about customer SLAs.

Immediate asks:
- Can Redwood provide a hot triage and an ops runbook for mitigation?
- Can you enable any temporary fallbacks (e.g., fallback to hosted model or older quantized variant) while we stabilize?
- We need a timeline for root cause and a proposal for durable fixes.

I've CC'd our infra lead, Alan Cho, for access coordination. We are ready to grant a temporary support tunnel if needed.

Attachments: auroraveil_kv_logs_1128.txt, cpu_profile_1129.json

Samantha Lowe
Head of Product Operations
Aurora Veil

- Tactical mitigation options to attempt during call: enable prefix K/V cache pinning, temporarily increase per-replica KV cache allocation from 4GB to 6GB, and increase batching window from 20ms to 40ms to reduce eviction churn.
- Fallback option: we can route a % of traffic to a hosted, Redwood-managed compatible model variant (same family, quantized) while we stabilize — requires your approval to re-route traffic.

Vivek, Rishi, Monica — tagging you for ops and billing coordination. Samantha, please confirm the on-call bridge details and whether you can open a support tunnel for us.

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Urgent — KV-cache starvation on our on-prem cluster (p99 spikes / 502s)

On Nov 28, 2026 15:45 PST, Samantha wrote:
> We're seeing a sustained degradation...

Summary of quick findings after initial log scan:
- Logs show frequent KV-cache evictions correlated with burst traffic; working set appears to exceed configured cache budget leading to cache thrashing.
- We also see GC/eviction events in the runtime that line up with high batching bursts.
- CPU profiles indicate short-lived high syscall latency on the host during those bursts (possible I/O contention).

Tactical mitigations we can apply immediately (low risk):
1) Increase KV cache allocation per replica (4GB -> 6GB) and restart replicas one at a time to avoid global cold-starts. Expected: immediate reduction in cache misses; risk: extra memory pressure on hosts.
2) Batching/window tuning: increase batching window (20ms -> 40ms) and cap max concurrent batches to reduce peak memory pressure. Expected: slight added latency tail for small requests, but significant reduction in load spikes.
3) Enable prefix pinning for critical request routes (customer-identified prefixes) to reduce eviction for hot keys.
4) If we continue to see kernel-level I/O contention, we will propose moving KV storage to tmpfs backed by higher-performance local NVMe (requires change window).

We can hot-patch the agent config and orchestrator during the call. Estimated cost impact: ~20-30% token processing cost increase for the incident window due to reduced packing efficiency.

I will prepare a CLI runbook and a one-page change plan. Need authorization to temporarily scale memory and to enable the hosted fallback routing (if Aurora approves).

Vivek
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-30T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-triage exec summary & next steps — Aurora Veil incident (RW-4821)

Samantha / Alan / Matthew — summary from our triage and the executive sync earlier today: 

What happened (short): KV-cache capacity on the on-prem replicas was insufficient for the higher working set during your traffic spike, producing cache thrashing, elevated p99 latency, and downstream 502s. We also observed transient host I/O contention that amplified evictions.

What we did (immediate):
- Applied KV cache increase to 6GB per replica, rolled one replica at a time to avoid mass cold starts.
- Increased batching window to 40ms and capped concurrency to smooth bursts.
- Enabled prefix pinning for top 20 prefixes identified by your team.
- Temporarily routed 25% of traffic to a Redwood-hosted compatible model variant to reduce peak working set while we stabilized.

Impact: p99 latency returned to under 600ms within the first 30 minutes and 502 rate dropped to <0.5% across endpoints. Throughput recovered to ~90% baseline. There is a temporary estimated cost uplift of ~22% for the incident window (we will reconcile final numbers).

Open actions and owners:
- Vivek: follow-up proposal for durable fix (NVMe-backed KV layer or increased host memory) + perf test by 2026-12-07. (Jira: RW-4821)
- Monica: collect and archive all change diffs and audit logs; write the postmortem draft. Due 2026-12-03.
- Rishi / Marissa: finalize incident credit worksheet and commercial offer for Aurora Veil (deliverable 2026-12-02).
- Aurora Veil: provide representative load tests and any additional hot prefixes to pin.

Next sync: We'll run a 30-minute follow-up on 2026-12-01 10:00 PST to review the durable remediation plan.

Attachments: sla_credit_request_form.pdf (we included the initial worksheet template).

Thanks again for the rapid coordination. We'll keep the hosted routing in place at 25% until your team validates the perf tests or we complete the NVMe migration.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
